correctness.rationale: Connected cuts with both induced sides connected classify all facets of a connected graphical zonotope; their Euclidean facet measures are sqrt(|S||T|) times the product of induced spanning-tree counts. The complete-split graph has exactly 2q peripheral-singleton directed facets and (2^p-2)2^q clique-splitting facets with the stated expressions. Matrix-tree gives τ(K_a∨I_b)=(a+b)^(a-1)a^(b-1), including a=1/b=0 boundary. Reweight the split-cut sum by T∼Bin(q,k/p), derive fixed-p expectation q^(p-1)(constant+O_p(q^-1)); divide by the 2q singleton area to obtain A_p q^-3/2+O_p(q^-5/2). For p→∞ express A_p/p^1.5 as two symmetric endpoint sums of binomial mass b_(p,k)/[k(1-k/p)]^1.5, dominate by O(k^-2) and use b_(p,k)→e^-k k^k/k!. This gives C*=∑ e^-j j^(j-3/2)/j!, not a simultaneous two-parameter limit.

value.rationale: This computes the complete intrinsic facet-area spectrum for a natural two-parameter family of graphical zonotopes, not just a combinatorial face count. A vanishing exponentially small fraction of singleton facets captures almost all boundary area, with a sharp family-dependent q^-3/2 deficit and an explicit nontrivial endpoint-Poisson limit as clique size grows. These results illuminate the mathematically meaningful contrast between uniform facet sampling and surface-area sampling.
